lineage agent notes: 1) claims_paid_eur takes stg.claim_payments.amount as-is. Despite the name, nothing converts it to EUR and claim_payments has no currency column. The same unconverted amount feeds paid_to_written and review_flag. 2) The stg.brokers LEFT JOIN doesn't remove rows, but brokers has a _row_seq column, so it may hold several versions per broker_code. If it does, output rows are duplicated. I listed the join as a low-confidence filter. 3) Claims count toward claims_notified, and their payments toward claims_paid_eur, only if reported_date falls in the year. Payments in the year on claims reported earlier are dropped. 4) If no fx rate is found for a non-EUR currency, the product is NULL and SUM skips it, so that premium is lost from gwp_eur without any error. 5) policies_in_force and claims_notified are COUNT(*) values defaulted to 0 by ISNULL, so they have no column that derives them. The in-force and claims date filters still decide which rows are counted. 6) The output's broker_code and lob_code are the union of keys across in-force, premium, notified and paid, so every filter on those sets helps decide which rows appear.

warnings:
lineage agent notes: The ROW_NUMBER at lines 76-77 groups by (period, claim_id) only, not by reserve_type. So each claim keeps just its single latest reserve row, whatever its type. The header says expense reserves count towards incurred (CR-0577), but they are only included when the expense reserve happens to be the latest row. The SUM at lines 85-86 then always adds up exactly one row per period. The PySpark version must copy this exactly, not fix it. Ties on reserve_date are broken by reserve_id DESC.

When computing last_payment_date, payments with a NULL amount are skipped (line 67), but they still count as nil in the sums.

days_since_last_activity is NULL when the claim has no payments and no reserves. The 1900-01-01 sentinel only affects the comparison and never reaches the output.

The filter edges on payment_date, reserve_date and the claim_id joins in the payment and reserve steps decide which payment and reserve rows feed the sums. They change which rows appear only indirectly, through the incurred_amount >= 25000 threshold at line 134.

warnings:
translator notes: 1. Ties in ROW_NUMBER with the same reserve_date and reserve_id are broken by ascending _row_seq. The legacy order is non-deterministic in that case.
2. The joins to #clm are kept as real joins rather than semi-joins, including the final #inc-to-#clm join. Duplicate claim_ids in stg.claims would multiply rows in the same way as in the legacy job.
3. The status filter uses upper(rtrim(status)), which reproduces case-insensitive, trailing-space-insensitive collation while leading spaces still count (X2-D3). LTRIM/RTRIM in the output columns map to F.trim, which trims spaces only.
4. Intermediate sums are cast to decimal(38,2) to match T-SQL's SUM type. The 1.10 and 0.90 multipliers are Decimal literals, so the comparison is exact.
5. The 1900-01-01 sentinel is built from the legacy literal '19000101' as a typed date.
